messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall - p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints using mixed-precision model variants (int8 + fp8). Alert: p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~950ms, p99 ~2.6s across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Streaming stall rate up ~6% in last 10m. Auto-escalation to sev-2. Thread started 2245012345

eric.oncall: on it. grabbing logs now. any recent deploys or quant profile changes?

maya.prod: we rolled int8 calibration profile to 75% at 02:14 UTC as part of the throughput cost opt. Canary looked ok, but we saw a handful of tail spikes at canary, rolled to 50% for a while.

ben.runtime: looking at runtime metrics: many calls show repeated dequant exceptions and KV cache misses when switching shards -> long GC-like stalls. CPU on host stays low, GPU utilization normal. kernel timings show an extra 200-800ms in dequant path for long-context requests.

ajay.ml: calibration job for int8 completed 02:10 but we had 3 calibration outliers flagged. Looks like fp8 fallbacks were skipped in route policy. I see last night's calibration job wrote new precision profile to model catalog: "mix-int8-fp8-v3".

anna-cs: CS reports 3 customers with SLO breaches and websocket disconnects. One midsize customer (search-as-a-service) reported multiple streaming stalls. On their side, client sees intermittent partial responses then reconnects.

eric.oncall: can we confirm scope? percent of total traffic hitting affected variants?

ben.runtime: query: routing table shows 18% of production traffic routed to mix-int8-fp8-v3. Most of the spikes come from long-ctx (>=1024 tokens) requests. Short requests fine.

nora-ops: posting recent traces: https://internal.trace/redwood/2245012345 - flamegraphs show long stall in dequant::apply_kv on a few hosts (host-rt-42, host-rt-57).

ben.runtime: repro snippet for the stall (from host-rt-57 logs):
```
[2026-03-15T02:20:11Z] request_id=xyz kv_cache_miss=true dequant_path=fp8_to_fp16 sync_wait=732ms dequant_errors=0
[2026-03-15T02:20:11Z] request_id=xyz kernels_taken=[softmax, matmul, dequant, attention] total_infer=1150ms p99
```

ajay.ml: hypothesis: new mixed profile triggers an extra dequant path when token types switch between segments -> inefficiency for long context. Calibration fallback rules were tightened which prevented automatic fallback to fp16 for those cases.

maya.prod: impact summary: ~12% of streaming p95/p99 across regions degraded, 4 customers > SLO, no data leakage. Severity remains sev-2 due to customer impact.

eric.oncall: immediate mitigation suggestions? options: 1) pause rollout (stop traffic to mix-int8-fp8-v3), 2) force route fallback to fp16 for long-context requests, 3) roll back model profile to previous stable. Thoughts?

ben.runtime: we can flip routing policy quickly: `redwoodctl routing set-priority mix-int8-fp8-v3=0 --unsafe` will force fallback to other variants. But safer: add rule: if request_len > 512 -> route to fp16. That patch can be applied to routing layer in <3m.

ajay.ml: rollback of catalog entry to mix-int8-fp8-v2 is possible but takes ~8-12m to fully drain and reroute due to sticky connections. Routing rule change is faster.

nora-ops: I've prepared a short mitigation playbook and will apply the >512 token routing rule now. Will monitor for 10m, then decide on rollback.

deploy-bot: action initiated by nora-ops: routing-rule-update --id=rr-20260315-01 --conditions="request_len>512" --target=fp16-variants --status=applying

ben.runtime: confirming hosts: injecting temporary throttle on host-rt-57 and host-rt-42 to reduce concurrent long-context queues while routing change propagates. Exec: `ssh host-rt-57 sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime && tc qdisc add dev eth0 handle 1:1 tbf rate 500mbit burst 32k latency 100ms` (measure only).

anna-cs: told affected customers we are investigating and applying a mitigation that may reduce throughput for long queries; offering expedited postmortem.

[~8 minutes pass]

nora-ops: routing rule applied. telemetrics: p95 dropped from ~950ms -> ~180ms in eu-west-1 within 90s. p99 trending down from 2.6s -> 420ms. streaming stall rate down to 0.9%.

maya.prod: good win. capture point: int8 calibration created a faster but fragile path for long contexts; fallback policy was too strict.

eric.oncall: next steps: (A) keep routing rule in place until we fully validate a repaired profile, (B) run a targeted calibration replay for long-context buckets, (C) prepare catalog rollback plan if profile repair fails. Assign owners.

ajay.ml: I will run calibration replay on a copy of v3 focused on >=1024 tokens, will add more aggressive fallback triggers for dequant latency >250ms. ETA 3h for a proper replay + validation tests.

ben.runtime: I'll open a runtime hotfix to make dequant path async for long contexts where feasible and add extra KV cache warmup on model load. ETA 6h for canary.

nora-ops: I'll keep routing rule in place and monitor for 2h, then handoff to next oncall at 2245012600.

anna-cs: follow-up: CS will email affected customers with mitigation summary and offer dedicated support during validation window.

eric.oncall: thanks team. transferring incident to next oncall. Handoff: incident remains sev-2 until replay validated or rollback. Next oncall: @eric.oncall -> @lucy.oncall for 02:50 UTC handoff. Add notes: routing-rule rr-20260315-01 active, hosts throttled host-rt-42/57, calibration replay in progress by ajay.ml.

deploy-bot: note created: incident/2245012345 - active routing rule rr-20260315-01 - mitigation applied - owner ajay.ml/ben.runtime - followup required.

lucy.oncall: ack and taking over at 2245012600. please DM if anything flares.

sre-bot: incident thread closed for initial mitigation window. Continue monitoring 2h.
